lawRefs: M.G.L. c. 62 s. 4 (5% Part B rate; 8.5% short-term capital gains; 4% surtax, threshold adjusted by the IRC 1(f) cost-of-living adjustment)
Mass. Const. amend. art. XLIV as amended in 2022 (Fair Share Amendment)
M.G.L. c. 62 s. 3(B)(b) (personal exemptions $4,400 / $6,800 / $8,800; $700 age 65+; $2,200 blind; $1,000 dependent)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed from the fetched source documents; sha256 (when filled) is of the canonical body. mass.gov blocks automated fetching (HTTP 403), so the 2026 surtax threshold of $1,107,750 (2025: $1,083,150) was confirmed through search-engine extracts of the mass.gov tax-rates page and a Bloomberg Tax report on DOR's draft 2026 withholding methods (https://news.bloombergtax.com/payroll/massachusetts-releases-draft-2026-withholding-methods); rates and exemption amounts were read from the statute at malegislature.gov (c. 62 ss. 3 and 4) and cross-checked against Tax Foundation 2026. Flat 5% on interest/dividends, Part B income (wages, pensions, etc.) and long-term capital gains; `surtax` is the additional 4% on taxable income above $1,107,750 (same threshold for every filing status; not doubled for joint filers). Special capital-gains regimes not modeled: short-term capital gains are taxed at 8.5%; long-term gains on collectibles at 12%. Massachusetts has no standard deduction and uses its own gross-income base rather than federal AGI/taxable income; startingPoint federalAGI is the closest approximation. personalExemption is the single/MFS amount of $4,400 (MFJ $8,800 = $4,400 per spouse); head of household is $6,800 (not expressible); age 65+ adds $700 per person (seniorExtraDeduction); blind adds $2,200; dependents $1,000 each. Other Massachusetts deductions and credits (e.g. the deduction for Social Security/retirement-system contributions, rent deduction, senior circuit-breaker credit) are not modeled. Social Security is not taxed. No general pension/IRA exclusion (retirementIncomeExclusion 0); certain government contributory pensions are exempt. Exemptions and the rate are fixed by statute (not indexed); only the surtax threshold is indexed annually.

flags.indexed: false for exemptions/rate; the surtax threshold IS indexed annually (IRC 1(f) COLA)
flags.personalExemption: HOH exemption is $6,800 (contract holds one per-person amount: $4,400)
